description: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two. Otherwise, return false. An integer n is a power of two if there exists an integer x such that n == 2^x.
intuition: A power of two in binary has exactly one bit set (like 1, 10, 100, 1000). The bit trick n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit. If the result is 0 and n is positive, there was only one set bit, confirming it's a power of two.
approach: A power of two has exactly one bit set in binary. Use the bit trick: n & (n - 1) == 0 removes the lowest set bit. If the result is 0 and n > 0, it is a power of two.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: n = 16

16 in binary = 00010000
15 in binary = 00001111
16 & 15 = 00000000 = 0
16 > 0 and 0 === 0 -> true

Output: true

---

Input: n = 6
6 in binary = 00000110
5 in binary = 00000101
6 & 5 = 00000100 = 4 (not 0)
4 !== 0 -> false

Output: false
explanation:
1. A power of two in binary has exactly one 1-bit (e.g., 1000).
2. n - 1 flips all bits below that 1-bit (e.g., 0111).
3. n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
4. If the result is 0, there was only one set bit: power of two.
5. Also check n > 0 since 0 and negative numbers are not powers of two.
hints: Powers of two have exactly one bit set in binary.
n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
If the result is 0 and n > 0, it is a power of two.
